chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Abu Ja'far, from Abu Qatadah Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Hafsh al-Qummi and Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said:

I asked him about the Dahiyyah (sacrifice of Eid al-Adha): if the one who slaughters it makes a mistake and mentions the name of someone other than the owner, does it count for the owner of the Dahiyyah? He said, 'Yes, for him is only what he intended.' And it is preferable that one begins in Mina with the slaughter before the shaving (of the head). He narrated that.

key_terms.الضَّحِيَّة: Dahiyyah, the sacrificial animal offered on Eid al-Adha
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a location near Mecca significant for Hajj rituals
key_terms.يُسَمِّي: To mention/call upon the name of (God or the owner)

ai.seo_question: Does a mistake in naming the owner during Eid sacrifice invalidate the act for the owner?
ai.summary: Transmitted through the chain of the Bani Hashim and Qummi scholars, this hadith clarifies that the validity of the Dahiyyah sacrifice hinges on the internal intention (niyyah) of the slaughterer rather than the precise verbal recitation, ensuring the reward reaches the intended owner despite minor errors. It further establishes a specific ritual sequence for Hajj, recommending that the sacrifice in Mina precedes the shaving of the head, reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the Imams regarding the completion of Hajj rites.
